generatedProse.concept-context: Psychology tasks rarely have one right route. A report can be structured in several ways, a research question approached with different designs, a problem framed through more than one theory. Thinking flexibly means producing a few of these approaches before you commit, then watching how your chosen approach goes. If it stalls, you amend it or switch, rather than forcing a design or structure that is not working.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students are set the same demanding report with a tight deadline.

Tom picks the first structure that comes to mind and commits to it. Half way through, the sections clearly do not hang together, but Tom pushes on the same way, hoping more effort will fix it. Time runs out with little to show. There was never a second structure to turn to.

Amara starts by jotting three ways the report could be organised, then tries the most promising one. Watching the argument stall, Amara stops, returns to the list, and switches to a structure that fits the evidence better. The report gets finished, because a change of course was always available.

Both students worked hard. Only Amara generated options and stayed ready to adapt, turning a stall into a switch rather than a dead end.
generatedProse.summary: Thinking flexibly in psychology has two parts: generating several approaches to a task before you commit, and monitoring your chosen approach so you can adapt or switch when it is not working. You can now produce more than one way into a report or design, watch how an approach is going, and change course with control rather than pushing on regardless. The next lesson turns creativity onto the material itself, bringing imagination to analysis.

check.body: In the worked example, what let Amara realise her first approach was not working?

items.text: She kept checking, as she worked, whether the structure was getting her anywhere.
She waited until the deadline to review the whole report.
She asked Tom what structure to use.
She had chosen only one structure from the start.

feedback.correct: That's right. Monitoring the work as she went is what let Amara spot the stall in time to switch.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. What was Amara doing while she worked that Tom was not?
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara kept checking, as she worked, whether her structure was getting anywhere. That monitoring revealed the stall in time to switch.
